description: Looping random sequencer built on a 16-bit shift register, with a voltage sequence, an inverted copy of it, a gate output for each of the sixteen bits, white noise and a clock copy

params.text: Holds the sequence while it is pressed by disconnecting the clock, and playback carries on from where it stopped when it is released
Generates one internal clock pulse, moving the sequence forward by one bit
While it is held, the first bit of the shift register is set to zero on each clock pulse, turning ones into zeroes
While it is held, the first bit of the shift register is set to one on each clock pulse, turning zeroes into ones
Sets the chance the last bit is inverted as it is copied back to the first: even at the centre, none at LIN so the loop repeats unaltered, and inversion every time round at CYC, doubling the loop
Sets the bit the sequence is copied back from, 1 to 16, which is the length of the loop
Scales the voltage at SEQ and INV SEQ, from -8V fully counter-clockwise to 8V fully clockwise

inputs.text: Each rising edge moves the shift register on by one bit; it counts as high from 2V upwards
Adds to the SHIFT knob, 5V here covering the knob's full travel
Adds to the BITS knob, at three bits per volt
Adds to the LEVEL knob, and the result is limited to the range -8V to 8V
A voltage of 2V or more sets the first bit of the shift register to zero on the next clock pulse
A voltage of 2V or more sets the first bit of the shift register to one on the next clock pulse

outputs.text: The first eight bits of the shift register read as a number from 0 to 255 and scaled by LEVEL, giving a new voltage on every clock pulse
The voltage at SEQ with its sign flipped
White noise from the module's own generator, running whether or not a clock is patched
Carries 8V while the signal at the CLOCK input is high
Carries 8V while that bit of the shift register is a one, for as long as the clock pulse lasts

notes: the contents of the shift register are saved with the patch, so a locked sequence comes back when the patch is reopened
the module has no clock of its own; the shift register moves only on a rising edge at CLOCK or a press of the STEP button
